Vaccinating SA part 2

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The first Covid-19 vaccines are here! We tell the inside story of how they will be distributed

Unique Selling Point:
The first million doses of the Astra Zeneca COVID-19 vaccines landed at OR Tambo this past Monday to much fanfare. Their arrival heralds the start of the most complex and ambitious vaccination programme in South African history. We track their journey: A multi-step process consisting of customs clearance, transportation to cold-storage warehouses, vaccine “quarantine” in parallel with independent laboratory verification and quality testing, and finally, vaccine shipments to points of use.

Summary:
At the beginning of the year we did a story about vaccinating SA.

Now at the start of February the first batch of vaccines have finally arrived in South Africa.

https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2021-01-31-covid-vaccines-to-land-in-south-africa-on-monday-we-break-down-what-will-happen-once-they-arrive/

https://www.timeslive.co.za/sunday-times/news/2021-01-31-health-minister-zweli-mkhize-lets-slip-covid-19-vaccine-surprise/


in this follow up, we tell the story of how this first batch of 1million doses will be distributed, by tracking the path of these vaccines from the their arrival at OR Tambo and all the intermediate steps on their journey to the arms of the first recipients - frontline healthcare workers

In an exclusive interview with Health Minister Zweli Mkhize, we get the low down on the government’s planned vaccination drive. This has already been described as the most complicated logistical project in South African history, so how is it going to work?

The government has an ambitious plan to inoculate 67% of the population by the end of the year. How achievable is this? We’ve already seen the slow pace of vaccinations in the EU where the consequences of vaccine nationalism is playing out via an ugly spat with the UK

We also outline the different types of vaccines that have been produced, how they differ from one another and which ones will be coming to South Africa

Finally we also speak with NICD’s Lynn Morris the implications of South African strain of SARS COV-2 on vaccine efficacy

Expert:
Dr. Zweli Mkhize
Prof. Lynn Morris
Dr. Morena Makhoana
Mr. Stavros Nicolaou Aspen

Press Release:


A year into the COVID-19 pandemic, that has killed 46 869 South Africans and counting, the rapid development of vaccines offers a route back to normality. When the first million doses of AstraZeneca vaccines landed at O.R. Tambo last week, hope was alive that the government’s ambitious drive to inoculate over 40 million people this year could finally begin. But then the disturbing news broke that the AstraZeneca vaccine is ineffective at preventing mild and moderate disease caused by the South African variant of COVID-19. Carte Blanche sits down with South Africa’s leading scientists and the Minister of Health Dr Zweli Mhkize to examine the way forward.

Script:



V/O A year into the COVID-19 pandemic, vaccines offer the only route back to normality.

So when the first million doses of AstraZeneca vaccines landed at OR Tambo last week Monday, hope was kindled.

PRESIDENT RAMAPHOSA SOUNDBYTE





V/O: South Africa plans to inoculate 40 million citizens in 2021 and was supposed to start this week, with frontline healthcare workers first in line to receive the jab.

Zweli Mkhize is the Minister of Health

Zweli on healthcare workers and on the urgency that is required


V/O: South Africa’s second deadly wave of COVID-19 has been driven by the 501Y.V2 variant which emerged last November.

Of even greater concern were mutations that made this new variant resistant to antibodies of the original strain -

Professor Lyn Morris from the NICD was alarmed by their lab tests

LYNN MORRIS: Why are scientists around the world so worried about this South African variant?

DEREK: Then this past Sunday devastating news: These vaccines have been shown to be ineffective at preventing mild and moderate disease caused by the South African variant of COVID-19.

ZWELI: I was devastated

South Africa’s leading epidemiologist Professor Salim Abdool Karim explains Prof Madhi’s results

PROF KARIM: Can you explain in layman’s terms what the research led by Professor Shabir Madhi actually showed?


V/O: This forced the South African government to pause the rollout of AstraZeneca vaccines this week

ZWELI: The AstraZeneca could not demonstrate…

V/O: So the decision was made to swap out AstraZeneca with vaccines made by Johnson & Johnson. Why?

Karim explain why and how the AstraZeneca vaccines will be swapped out with Johnson & Johnson

V/O: Local company Aspen will be manufacturing Johnson & Johnson vaccines in Port Elizabeth. Could South Africa get access to this supply?

Zweli on Aspen and whether SA will get access to this supply



V/O: The government hopes to begin vaccinating healthcare workers next week – the first phase of an ambitious rollout that will be the largest in our history and will require partnership with big business.

Stavros Nicolau is head of the health working group of Business for South Africa


Stavros on business’ role
V/O: One of the key partners in the first phase of the vaccination drive is the Biovac Institute.

LINK 2: I’m here at the Biovac Institute who have been tasked with storing and transporting the millions of doses of vaccines. It’s a mammoth undertaking

V/O: DR Morena Makhoana is their CEO

MORENA MAKHOANA: What is the role that Biovac will play in South Africa’s COVD-19 Vaccination Drive?
Morena explains the cold storage chain














V/O: When vaccines land in the country, they will be transported from OR Tambo to Biovac’s facilities in Johannesburg. There they will be quarantined in cold storage rooms (which are kept at between 2 to 8 degrees Celsius).

After independent lab verification and quality testing, the batch is ready for distribution.

V/O: The vaccines will be covered in thermal blankets before being taken from the cold rooms to the trucks, ready to be transported to hundreds of destinations all over the country.


DEREK: What will become of the million doses of AstraZeneca vaccine?

Karim on collecting the data

V/O: With the virus shown to be constantly mutating, is herd immunity still achievable?

Prof Karim on herd immunity: we need to answer the question of: can a vaccinated person transmit the disease?
We are going to have to live with COVID for the next 2-3 years
V/O: With winter just a few months away and warnings from scientists of an imminent 3rd wave, the race is on to vaccinate as many South Africans as possible
CLOSING COMMENT FROM ZWELI MKHIZE: Many South Africans are disheartened about the news and could lose faith in the vaccination drive. What words of encouragement do you have that could restore confidence?



PROMO 1: As vaccines begin to arrive in the country, disturbing news: They are not as effective against the South African variant of COVID-19. What are the implications for SA’s vaccination drive?


PROMO 2: SA’s vaccination drive was meant to start this week. But news that the AstraZeneca vaccine has limited efficacy against the South African variant paused the rollout. So what happens now?

Promo 3: SA’s COVID-19 vaccine drive will be the largest in our history. We take you inside the logistical challenges required to vaccinate millions of citizens this year alone.
